divergence_from_worker_builder.note: Not a length difference — a type contradiction. The worker puts state here; the browser puts null.
The context block. The central open question of this measurement.
32 hex chars — conversationId. Confirmed against the response body, which carries ["c_1055552f96923f8c", "r_6e83cca9edc47aee"].
'notebooks/' (9) + uuid (36) = 45. One character away. Candidate for the notebook reference, but NOT confirmed by a grounded/ungrounded pair yet.

classifier_gap.finding: STRING_CLASS.NOTEBOOK_REF matches the prefix 'notebook://' — with a scheme separator. The payload carries 'notebooks/' without one, so a notebook reference would classify as 'opaque'.
classifier_gap.consequence: KAN-195's grounded-vs-ungrounded comparison could see only a LENGTH difference, because the classifier could not report the one bit that distinguishes them. That is precisely the ambiguity that test file was written to fix, and the fix does not cover the real prefix.
classifier_gap.status: hypothesis — needs the ungrounded-notebook capture to confirm

context_block_reading: Length varies with conversation length, which argues against a fixed server-issued nonce. Whether it can be reconstructed from known inputs is UNKNOWN and is the thing step 5 of the plan was written to settle.

structural_finding.finding: The notebook page does not host a conversation. Asking a question there GETs /notebook/b55f1ee0-... and the browser then issues GET https://gemini.google.com/app, spawning a NEW conversation under /app/<new-id>. Every conversation that has ever carried a notebook reference therefore lives under /app.
structural_finding.consequence: There is no distinct 'ungrounded-notebook' surface to capture. The notebook reference is not a property of the PAGE, it is a property of the CHIP attached inside an /app conversation. The comparison the plan needs is therefore chip-present vs chip-absent WITHIN /app, not notebook-page vs app-page.
structural_finding.implication_for_capture_plan: The four planned cases collapse to three: an /app turn with a fresh chip, an /app turn with no chip, and a repeat to see the context block grow. This also explains why set_bridge_scope('notebook:...') navigates away from the chat surface entirely.

still_missing: grounded-notebook — captured indirectly: horo_consult returned verified:true with citationCount 14, but the payload probe was off by then because set_bridge_scope reloads the page and resets payloadProbeEnabled
grounded-notebook-repeat — attempted; the prompt did not reach Gemini (collect_answer_timeout, responses on screen=2), so no request was emitted
ungrounded-notebook — requires asking on the notebook page WITHOUT attaching the chip, which horo_consult never does because attaching is its job
method_note: Kapture network_monitor turned out to be the better capture path: it survives navigation, needs no page-side toggle, and yields the raw f.req rather than only its shape. The PAYLOAD_PROBE was designed to be console-only under GUARDRAILS G1.2.1, which is correct for a shipped build — but it also means every navigation costs a manual re-enable.

notebook_binding_field.evidence: Two turns in two DIFFERENT conversations - the [4] conversationId fingerprints differ (09b7b2e5 vs ac1eae62), so the 88-char field matching (cff9779e) is not an artifact of the same conversation. The empty 0-char and 4-char siblings at [0][3][0][0][3] and [0][3][0][1] are likewise stable.

whatItIsNot.notebook_uri: no notebooks:// - which is why classifyString never flagged it

notebook_binding_field.interpretation: An opaque per-notebook token, stable for the notebook rather than the session. Reproducible by a builder for a KNOWN notebook; not derivable without observing it once.
notebook_binding_field.openGap: contains.notebook_id came back null on both turns: the worker derives the id from currentScope, but attach-in-place keeps the scope at app:*, so the notebook id is not in the scope string. The comparison was never actually run.
